rules.title: Integer-class type kinds
rules.statement: The integer type class comprises the fixed-width signed/unsigned kinds {i8,u8,i16,u16,i24,u24,i32,u32,i56,u56,i64,u64,i128,u128}, the pointer-sized {usize,isize}, the unsuffixed-literal type IntLit, and Enum. An enum type is treated as an integer kind for these classifications.
rules.divergence: Logos adds non-power-of-two integer widths i24/u24/i56/u56 (not in Rust); also classifies Enum as an integer kind.
rules.uncertainty: Whether Enum membership here reflects a general language rule or only this classifier's use sites is not determinable from this unit alone.

rules.title: Integer bit-width and signedness
rules.statement: Each concrete integer kind has a fixed bit width and signedness: i8/u8=8, i16/u16=16, i24/u24=24, i32/u32=32, i56/u56=56, i64/u64=64, i128/u128=128; signed forms are signed, unsigned forms unsigned. usize/isize have width equal to the target pointer width (isize signed, usize unsigned). IntLit, Enum, and non-integers have no defined rank (width 0).
rules.divergence: usize/isize width is target-dependent (pointer bits) as in Rust; the exotic 24/56-bit widths are a Logos addition.

rules.title: Safe implicit integer widening
rules.statement: An implicit integer widening from `from` to `to` is permitted iff every value of `from` is representable in `to`: signed->signed and unsigned->unsigned require to_width >= from_width; unsigned->signed requires to_width > from_width; signed->unsigned is never permitted. usize/isize are distinct types: no implicit conversion between a pointer-sized integer and any fixed-width integer (only psize<->psize among themselves). Either operand having undefined rank (IntLit/Enum/non-integer) blocks widening.
rules.divergence: Rust performs NO implicit integer widening at all (requires explicit `as`). Logos permits value-preserving implicit widening here.

rules.title: Unsuffixed integer literal unifies to the other operand's type
rules.statement: When unifying two integer types, if one is the unsuffixed literal type IntLit it unifies to the other operand's type. Otherwise the narrower is widened to the wider when a safe implicit widening exists (per coerce.int.implicit-widening); if neither widens, the first operand's type is kept.

rules.title: Numeric literal (int or float) unifies to the concrete operand
rules.statement: When unifying two numeric types where either operand may be a literal, an unsuffixed IntLit or FloatLit operand unifies to the other operand's (concrete) type; FloatLit thereby promotes to a concrete float type F32/F64.

rules.title: Constant integer-literal value extraction through block/negation
rules.statement: A constant integer value is extracted from an expression by: unwrapping a block expression to its result subexpression; folding a unary `-` applied to a constant integer to its negation; and reading the value of an integer literal. Any other expression form has no constant integer value.

rules.title: Integer-literal range fit per target type
rules.statement: A constant integer value v fits a target integer kind iff it lies within that kind's representable range: i8 [-128,127], u8 [0,255], i16 [-32768,32767], u16 [0,65535], i24 [-2^23,2^23-1], u24 [0,2^24-1], i32 [INT32_MIN,INT32_MAX], u32 [0,UINT32_MAX], i56 [-2^55,2^55-1], u56 [0,2^56-1], i64/i128/isize(64-bit) all int64 values, u64/u128/usize require v>=0. On a 32-bit target usize requires v in [0,UINT32_MAX] and isize in [INT32_MIN,INT32_MAX].

rules.title: Unsuffixed integer literal must fit i64/u64 (64-bit) magnitude
rules.statement: An integer literal's magnitude is rejected if it exceeds 64-bit representable range: an unsigned magnitude must fit u64; a negated literal's magnitude must not exceed 2^63 (INT64_MIN is representable, anything past overflows). Literals are parsed in base 10, or 0x/0X hex, 0b/0B binary, 0o/0O octal, with `_` digit separators ignored; parsing stops at the first character that is not a valid digit for the base (the type suffix).
rules.divergence: Rust default integer literal type is i32; here the raw overflow bound is 64-bit (i64/u64), with per-suffix bounds layered at the call site.

rules.title: Integer literal radix prefixes and digit separators
rules.statement: Integer literals support an optional leading `-`, the radix prefixes 0x/0X (hex), 0b/0B (binary), 0o/0O (octal), default decimal, and `_` digit separators which are ignored in the value. Digits outside the active base terminate the numeric body (beginning the optional suffix).

rules.title: 128-bit integer literal magnitude
rules.statement: An integer literal targeting i128/u128 is accumulated as a 128-bit unsigned magnitude (sign applied by the caller) and is rejected only if its magnitude exceeds 128 bits; 64-bit-overflowing values round-trip intact.
rules.divergence: Logos provides i128/u128 literals; magnitude bound is 128 bits rather than 64.

rules.title: Digit-separator `_` placement validity
rules.statement: A `_` digit separator is valid only between two digits: it may not be the first or last character of a digit group, and consecutive `__` separators are forbidden. A digit group containing any character not accepted by its radix predicate is invalid.
rules.uncertainty: Rust permits leading/trailing and repeated underscores in some positions; exact conformance not confirmed from this unit.

rules.title: Well-formed integer literal grammar
rules.statement: A valid integer literal = optional `-`, then either a radix-prefixed body (0x hex / 0b binary / 0o octal) or a decimal body, with valid digit-separator placement, optionally followed by exactly one recognised integer suffix from {usize,isize,i128,i64,i56,i32,i24,i16,i8,u128,u64,u56,u32,u24,u16,u8}.

rules.title: Well-formed float literal grammar
rules.statement: A valid float literal = optional `-`, then a mantissa with either (a) a decimal point `.` with valid digit groups before and after, or (b) no decimal point but a mandatory exponent (e/E with optional +/- and digits) — a bare integer with no point and no exponent is NOT a float literal — optionally with an e/E exponent in case (a), and optionally followed by exactly one float suffix f32 or f64.

rules.title: Integer literal type suffix
rules.statement: An integer literal may carry an explicit type suffix selecting its kind: i8/i16/i24/i32/i56/i64/i128, u8/u16/u24/u32/u56/u64/u128, usize, isize; the suffix follows the (optionally radix-prefixed) digit body. Absence of a recognised suffix yields the unsuffixed literal type.
rules.divergence: Includes Logos-specific suffixes i24/u24/i56/u56 absent in Rust.

rules.title: Float literal type suffix
rules.statement: A float literal may carry the suffix f32 or f64 selecting F32/F64; absence yields the unsuffixed float-literal type.
